meta.inclusion_criteria: Crops developed using site-directed nucleases (ZFN/TALEN/CRISPR), oligo-directed mutagenesis, or editing-derived cisgenesis, regardless of whether a transgene remains in the final line. Classical transgenic GM crops (random insertion by e.g. Agrobacterium or biolistics, with no site-directed nuclease) are excluded. NOTE: inclusion is decided on METHOD; the resulting product's transgene status is recorded separately in edit.transgene_status because it is of interest to users.
meta.scope_note: Focus is on authorisation/clearance to cultivate or commercialise in the country where the crop is grown. Import- and food/feed-only authorisations are excluded. In the United States most editions receive a 'non-regulated' determination rather than an affirmative approval; this is captured in each approval's 'mechanism' field.

field_definitions.edit.transgene_status: transgene_free | contains_transgene | null_segregant | unknown. Records the OUTCOME of the final line, independent of the editing method used.
field_definitions.approvals.mechanism: affirmative_approval | non_regulated_determination | exemption | notification | unknown. How the clearance was granted. Distinguishing these matters for honest counting/mapping: an affirmative authorisation (e.g. Brazil CTNBio), a case-by-case determination of non-regulation (e.g. US APHIS 'Am I Regulated?'), an exemption, and a mandatory notification-that-deems-non-GMO (e.g. Japan MHLW/MAFF) are legally different events.
field_definitions.approvals.decision_date: Date or year of the government regulatory determination/clearance. LEFT BLANK where the exact date cannot be confirmed from a reliable source.
field_definitions.approvals.commercial_status: marketed | early_commercialisation | approved_not_marketed | withdrawn | unknown. The market reality in THIS country.
field_definitions.approvals.commercial_since: Year (or date) the crop was first grown/marketed in THIS country. Blank if not yet on-market or unknown.
field_definitions.coverage_notes: Top-level array recording jurisdictions searched that yielded NO qualifying crop records, so that a confirmed absence is distinguishable from an unsearched country. framework_stance summarises the regulatory posture (permissive | case_by_case_permissive | export_only | restrictive | moratorium_with_emerging_carveout | constitutional_constraint_with_carveout | prohibition).
field_definitions.location: Added for mapping purposes (not in the original source dataset). Approximate coordinates of the developer's headquarters/origin city, used to place a single point marker per innovation. Not the precise field/cultivation site.

trait.description: Elevated oleic acid (~80%) with reduced saturated and trans fat, yielding a more stable, trans-fat-free cooking oil.

approvals.notes: First gene-edited food commercialised in the US (Calyno oil, launched 2019; FAD2-1A/1B knockout). APHIS 'Am I Regulated?' non-regulated determination was issued for the original high-oleic soybean (Calyxt's lead product, predating its Feb-2016 powdery-mildew-wheat letter) but the EXACT DATE is not confirmed from a reliable source, so decision_date is intentionally left blank. Do NOT confuse with Calyxt's separate high-oleic/low-linolenic (HOLL) soybean, which was deemed non-regulated on 2020-06-03 but never commercialised. FDA voluntary consultation completed (BNF 000164).

location.place: Durham, North Carolina, US (approximate — developer HQ)

trait.description: Reduced pungency/bitterness for palatability while retaining the nutritional profile of mustard greens (marketed as 'Purple Power Baby Greens').

approvals.notes: First CRISPR-edited food product on the US market. USDA/APHIS confirmed non-regulated status mid-August 2020; foodservice launch May 2023, retail rollout later in 2023. Exact APHIS letter date to be confirmed against the primary APHIS response.

location.place: St. Louis, Missouri, US (approximate — developer HQ)

trait.description: Reduced erucic acid (from >35% to <2%) and reduced seed fibre/shatter, domesticating pennycress as a winter oilseed cover crop for food/feed and biofuel feedstock.

approvals.notes: Deregulated by USDA; first commercialisation efforts began 2023. Combines CRISPR edits with conventional breeding. Exact APHIS determination date and the transgene status of the marketed line still TO CONFIRM against primary sources.

location.place: Tsukuba, Japan (approximate — developer HQ / university spin-out origin)

trait.description: Elevated GABA (gamma-aminobutyric acid), 4-6x conventional levels, via knockout of the autoinhibitory domain of glutamate decarboxylase (GAD). Marketed with functional-food claims (blood pressure/relaxation).

developer.name: Sanatech Seed Co., Ltd. (University of Tsukuba spin-out; sales via Pioneer EcoScience)

approvals.notes: World's first commercialised genome-edited food crop. Under Japan's 2019 guidelines, SDN-1 products with no foreign DNA are not treated as GMOs but require notification to MHLW and an information filing with MAFF; notification accepted 11 Dec 2020. Seedlings distributed to home gardeners May 2021; fruit commercial sales from 15 Sept 2021. Later certified a Food with Functional Claims by the Consumer Affairs Agency on 30 Nov 2022 (Notification H617). Sold only in Japan. NOTE: two genome-edited fish (red sea bream; tiger puffer - Regional Fish Institute) are also marketed in Japan but are excluded from this CROP catalogue.

coverage_notes.key_instrument: Gene Technology Regulations 2001 (amended Oct 2019); FSANZ GM-food definition narrowed June 2025
coverage_notes.explanation: SDN-1 editions are not regulated as GMOs and FSANZ excludes transgene-free SDN-1 from GM-food classification, yet no gene-edited crops are commercially cultivated in Australia as of 2025 (field trials only). Confirmed de facto absence under a permissive framework.

coverage_notes.key_instrument: HSNO Act 1996; Gene Technology Bill 2024 (in passage)
coverage_notes.explanation: All gene-editing techniques treated as genetic modification and tightly regulated by the EPA - a de facto ~30-year barrier. No GE crops grown commercially and no environmental-release applications filed. Liberalising Gene Technology Bill 2024 reported back by Select Committee 10 Oct 2025, second reading pending - status evolving, reconfirm before publication.

World's first NBT framework and regional model. CONABIA has issued numerous 'non-GMO' determinations (e.g. Neocrop high-fibre/amylose wheat, Sept 2025), but a non-GMO determination is a regulatory classification, not evidence of commercial cultivation - most determined products are advanced lines still heading to the field. No gene-edited crop confirmed as commercially cultivated as of the search date. NOTE: Argentina's flagship 'GM wheat' HB4 is TRANSGENIC (inserted sunflower HaHB4 gene) and is therefore out of scope; it should not be recorded as a gene-edited crop.

Extensive pipeline of CTNBio 'non-GMO/conventional' determinations under RN16 (e.g. Embrapa drought-tolerant and lectin-free soybeans; Cana Flex CRISPR sugarcane; FuturaGene gene-edited eucalyptus classified conventional Feb 2026, proceeding via field trials). Analyses cite a ~2-3 year lag from determination to market. No gene-edited crop confirmed as commercially cultivated as of the search date. CORRECTION FLAG: the widely-cited 'December 2024 MARA five biosafety certificates including the first gene-edited rice for domestic cultivation' is CHINA (MARA = China's Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Affairs, 31 Dec 2024), NOT Brazil - do not attribute this event to Brazil.

coverage_notes.key_instrument: SAG Resolution No. 1523/2001; 2017 NBT case-by-case approach
coverage_notes.explanation: SAG treats edits with no 'new combination of genetic material' as non-GMO on a case-by-case basis, but Chile's model is structurally export-oriented: environmental release of GE seed is permitted only for seed multiplication that is re-exported, not for domestic commercial cultivation. Chile is a major GE seed exporter (5th largest seed producer globally) but grows no gene-edited crop for domestic commercial use. Zero qualifying records by design.

coverage_notes.key_instrument: ICA Resolution 29299/2018, superseded/broadened by ICA Resolution 00022991 (11 Nov 2022)
coverage_notes.explanation: Case-by-case procedure; only products with stable foreign genetic material are classified as LMOs, transgene-free edits handled as conventional. Framework resembles the Argentine text. No gene-edited crop confirmed as commercially cultivated as of the search date.

coverage_notes.key_instrument: 2019 framework (Resolution of CONBIO; commonly cited as Res. 565/019, sometimes 842/2019)
coverage_notes.explanation: Case-by-case procedure exempting transgene-free edits from GMO regulation, in the Argentine mould. Instrument number is cited inconsistently across sources and should be confirmed against the primary Paraguayan resolution. No gene-edited crop confirmed as commercially cultivated as of the search date.

coverage_notes.key_instrument: Gene Editing Decree No. 84/024, announced 18 March 2024
coverage_notes.explanation: Most recent South American entrant to formalise an NBT/gene-editing framework (2024). Framework new; no gene-edited crop confirmed as commercially cultivated as of the search date.

coverage_notes.key_instrument: Constitution Art. 401 (GMO-free country, 2008); Organic Code of the Environment 2019; Ministerial Agreement No. 063 (precision-breeding technical guide)
coverage_notes.explanation: Constitution declares Ecuador GMO-free, creating a structural ceiling. Sub-constitutional instruments exempt transgene-free edited products by defining only recombinant/foreign-DNA organisms as GMOs. First application under this route submitted Oct 2024 (gene-edited banana for Fusarium wilt TR4 resistance) - application stage, not commercial cultivation. The 'Ecuador banana paradox': exemption rests on definitional exclusion rather than legislative authorisation.

coverage_notes.key_instrument: Law 29811 (2011) LMO moratorium, extended by Law 31111 to 31 Dec 2035; Ministerial Resolution D000068-2026-MINAM-DM (8 Mar 2026)
coverage_notes.explanation: Peru maintains a moratorium on the entry/production of Living Modified Organisms until end-2035. A March 2026 MINAM resolution establishes criteria to determine whether NBT/gene-edited products fall within the moratorium as LMOs; transgene-free edits not meeting the LMO definition may be treated as conventional. De jure moratorium with an emerging carve-out; no commercial cultivation of gene-edited crops.

GMO activity is heavily restricted and politically contested; GM soybean is the only transgenic crop commercially cultivated, and there is no operative framework enabling commercial cultivation of gene-edited crops (some sources characterise Bolivia's stance as an effective ban). No gene-edited crop commercially cultivated.

coverage_notes.key_instrument: Prohibition on environmental release of GMOs (biodiversity-conservation grounds)
coverage_notes.explanation: Environmental release of GMOs is prohibited; the country relies on GM food/feed imports from neighbours. No enabling framework for, or commercial cultivation of, gene-edited crops.
